quirks: Rochdale St Chad ancient parish straddles Lancashire and Yorkshire — part of the parish is in the West Riding of Yorkshire (Agbrigg wapentake). Search both Lancashire AND Yorkshire records for events in this parish; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rochdale_St_Chad,_Lancashire,_England_Genealogy

Civil registration began 1 July 1837 at the local registrar level (Rochdale Registration District); registration was not universally complied with until penalties were imposed in 1875. For births 1858–1874, check both GRO indexes and parish baptism registers as a cross-check; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration

Rochdale had approximately 20 chapelries within St Chad's parish boundary. If a family event is not found in the mother church registers, search the specific chapelry (Spotland, Wardleworth, Castleton, Smallbridge, Milnrow, etc.) — each kept its own baptism and burial registers; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rochdale_St_Chad,_Lancashire,_England_Genealogy

Two free civil registration indexes exist for Lancashire: FreeBMD (nationwide, July 1837–1940+: freebmd.org.uk) and LancashireBMD (county-specific copies of registration district certificates, births 1837–1974, marriages 1837–2010, deaths 1837–1975: lancashirebmd.org.uk). Search both — they are independent and each may surface entries the other misses.

The 1911 census used original household schedules (not copied by enumerators) and uniquely records the number of children born alive, still living, and deceased for each married woman — directly relevant to questions about a couple's children; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Census

Nonconformist denominations were very strong in Rochdale (Baptists, Independents, Methodists, Quakers, Roman Catholics). If a family is not found in Church of England registers, search Lancashire Non-Conformist Church Records (FamilySearch collection 3656808) and Lancashire Catholic Registers 1762-1913 (Ancestry collection 62472).

Marriage certificates post-1837 record ages, fathers' names, and occupations of both parties — valuable for tracing fathers and confirming family relationships. Anglican church marriage registers after 1837 are exact duplicates of civil certificates and may be freely consulted without ordering a GRO certificate; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration
Probate jurisdiction for Rochdale was the Court of the Bishop of Chester (Episcopal Consistory); for Lancashire probate records see https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lancashire_Probate_Records

# Locality Guide: Rochdale, Lancashire, England (1858–1911)

## Jurisdictional Context

Rochdale is an ancient market town in Lancashire, historically part of the ancient parish of **St Chad, Rochdale** (parish registers from 1582, Bishop's Transcripts from 1599). The parish straddles two counties: it is chiefly in the **Salford Hundred of Lancashire** but partly in the **Agbrigg wapentake of the West Riding of Yorkshire** — meaning records may be filed under either county. The civil **Rochdale Registration District** (and partly **Todmorden Registration District**) was created in 1837 when civil registration began. Ecclesiastically, Rochdale is in the Diocese of Manchester, Province of York. The archive for physical Lancashire records is the **Lancashire Record Office**.

Rochdale is an industrial town that grew rapidly during the textile (cotton/wool) industry; its population was ~25,000 in 1851 and grew substantially through the later 19th century.

---

## Civil Registration (from 1 July 1837)

Births, marriages, and deaths were registered at the Rochdale Registration District from 1 July 1837. Coverage was not universal until mandatory penalties in 1875; for births before 1875, cross-check parish baptism registers.

**Key online indexes (all periods 1858–1911 covered):**
- **FamilySearch** — England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837–2008 (collection 2285338); Marriage Registration Index, 1837–2005 (collection 2285732); Death Registration Index, 1837–2007 (collection 2285341) — all name-indexed, free
- **FreeBMD** (freebmd.org.uk) — free nationwide GRO index, July 1837–1940+
- **LancashireBMD** (lancashirebmd.org.uk) — free county-wide index of Rochdale district certificates: births 1837–1974, marriages 1837–2010, deaths 1837–1975
- **Ancestry** — Civil Registration Birth Index 1837–1915 (collection 8912); Marriage Index 1837–1915 (collection 8913); Death Index 1837–1915 (collection 8914) — indexed ($)
- **GRO** (gro.gov.uk) — free searchable births and deaths index; paid certificate ordering

**What certificates contain:**
- Birth: child's name, date/place, father's name and occupation, mother's full name including maiden name
- Marriage: names, ages, marital condition, occupations, residences, fathers' names and occupations, witnesses
- Death: name, age, occupation, cause of death, informant

---

## Census Records (1861–1911)

All England and Wales censuses 1861–1911 are indexed and online:

| Census | FamilySearch Collection | Access |
|--------|------------------------|--------|
| 1861 | 1493747 | Free (FS) — indexed & images |
| 1871 | 1538354 | Free (FS) — indexed & images |
| 1881 | 2562194 | Free (FS) — indexed & images |
| 1891 | 1865747 | Free (FS) — indexed & images |
| 1901 | 1888129 | Free (FS) — indexed & images |
| 1911 | 1921547 | Free (FS) — indexed & images |

Also at Ancestry, Findmypast, MyHeritage (all $). The **1911 census** is especially valuable: it preserved original household forms and asked each married woman how many children were born alive, how many were still living, and how many had died — directly relevant to questions about a couple's children.

Censuses 1851–1901 record: name, relationship to head, marital condition, age, occupation, and parish/county of birth.

---

## Church Records

**Rochdale St Chad parish registers begin 1582**; Bishop's Transcripts from 1599. The parish had ~20 chapelries with their own baptism and burial registers — search the specific chapelry if events are not in the St Chad mother church records.

**Church of England — key online collections:**
- **England, Lancashire, Parish Registers 1538–1910** (FamilySearch collection 1465701) — indexed & images, **free**
- Lancashire, England, Church of England Births and Baptisms, 1813–1911 (Ancestry collection 2575) — indexed & images ($)
- Lancashire, England, Church of England Marriages and Banns, 1754–1936 (Ancestry collection 2576) — indexed & images ($)
- Lancashire, England, Church of England Deaths and Burials, 1813–1986 (Ancestry collection 2577) — indexed & images ($)
- **Lancashire Online Parish Clerks** (lan-opc.org.uk) — free transcripts/abstracts for many Rochdale parishes
- **FreeReg** (freereg.org.uk) — free index of parish registers

**Nonconformist records** (very important for Rochdale — strong Baptist, Methodist, Independent, Quaker and Catholic communities):
- England, Lancashire Non-Conformist Church Records, 1647–1996 (FamilySearch collection 3656808) — indexed, free
- Lancashire, England, Non-Conformist Registers of Baptisms, Marriages and Burials, 1762–2005 (Ancestry collection 62471) — ($)
- Lancashire, England, Catholic Registers of Baptisms, Marriages and Burials, 1762–1913 (Ancestry collection 62472) — ($)

---

## Cemetery and Burial Records

- Rochdale Cemetery, Register of Burials, 1855–1999 (FamilySearch Catalog 1003215) — images
- Multiple Rochdale chapel burial grounds in FamilySearch Catalog (Spotland, West Street Baptist, Friends, etc.)
- Lancashire County Cemetery Records at interment.net — index
- National Burial Index for England & Wales at Findmypast — index ($)

---

## Key Repositories

- **Lancashire Record Office** (Preston) — physical parish registers, bishop's transcripts, court records, probate records
- **FamilySearch** — major Lancashire collections online, free
- **FreeBMD / LancashireBMD** — free civil registration indexes
- **Ancestry / Findmypast** — additional Lancashire collections ($)
- **Lancashire Online Parish Clerks** (lan-opc.org.uk) — free local transcripts

---

## Research Quirks

1. **Lancashire/Yorkshire split:** Part of Rochdale St Chad parish is in Yorkshire — search both county records.
2. **20 chapelries:** Each chapelry kept its own registers; events not in St Chad's mother church may be in a chapelry register.
3. **Two civil registration indexes:** Search both FreeBMD and LancashireBMD — they are independent and complementary.
4. **Pre-1875 birth registration gaps:** Cross-check baptism registers for births before 1875.
5. **1911 census:** Uniquely records children born alive/still living for each married couple.
6. **Strong Nonconformist community:** Always search Nonconformist registers alongside Church of England.

entry.rationale: Identity and parentage confirmation plan for Robert Brierley (b. 1858, Rochdale) who appears in the 1911 census and is hypothesised to be the same person as Robert Lord (b. 1858, son of Abel Brierley) in the tree. The surname discrepancy (tree: 'Lord'; census: 'Brierley') is a key issue — the birth registration should clarify whether 'Lord' is the mother's maiden name or otherwise connected. Plan traces Robert from birth through 1911 using civil registration, census, and church records, with Abel Brierley's household as the FAN anchor. Locality guide loc_001 (Rochdale, Lancashire, England, 1858–1911) applied throughout. Variant spellings to watch: Brierley / Brearley / Brierlay / Briarley; Lord variants unlikely to affect a birth registered under father's Brierley surname.

The question asserts Robert Brierley was enumerated at Rochdale in 1911 with wife Ellen and children James and Betsy. This item formally retrieves and extracts that census entry. The 1911 schedule (FamilySearch collection 1921547) used original household forms, records the head's age (should be ~53 if born 1858), birthplace, years of marriage, and number of children born alive and surviving — directly relevant to both the identity and children questions. Search for 'Robert Brierley' in Rochdale Registration District.

Primary direct evidence for the parentage claim. A GRO birth certificate for Robert Brierley born 1858 in the Rochdale Registration District should name his father (Abel Brierley) and mother, providing primary information from the birth informant. The mother's maiden name on the certificate may be 'Lord,' which would explain why the tree records him as 'Robert Lord.' Search England and Wales Birth Registration Index 1837–2008 (FamilySearch collection 2285338); also check FreeBMD (freebmd.org.uk) and LancashireBMD (lancashirebmd.org.uk births 1837–1974), both free. Per loc_001, registration was not universal before 1875 — if not found, fall through to pli_009 (church baptism).

FAN item targeting Abel Brierley's household. Robert, born 1858, would be approximately 3 years old in 1861; finding him enumerated as Abel Brierley's son in the 1861 census (FamilySearch collection 1493747) constitutes direct evidence of the parent–child relationship. The 1861 census records name, age, relationship to head of household, marital condition, occupation, and parish/county of birth. Also establishes Abel Brierley's location (expected: Rochdale area), which anchors the family geographically. Search for 'Abel Brierley' as head in Rochdale Registration District.

Traces Robert Brierley (age ~13) still in Abel's household in 1871, or nearby, strengthening the continuous family link. The 1871 census (FamilySearch collection 1538354) records relationship to head and birthplace. Consistent Rochdale birthplace across census years would confirm the same individual. Search for Abel Brierley's household and/or Robert Brierley age ~13 in Rochdale Registration District.

By 1881 Robert would be ~23 and may have left Abel's household. The 1881 census (FamilySearch collection 2562194) will locate him as a young adult — either still with Abel or establishing his own household, potentially indicating when he married Ellen. Birthplace should read Rochdale (or Rochdale Registration District). Variant spellings (Brearley, Brierlay) should be tried.

Marriage registration for Robert Brierley and Ellen. GRO marriage certificates after 1837 name the fathers of both parties — this would confirm Abel Brierley as Robert's father independently of the birth certificate, and supply Ellen's maiden name. Date range estimated: Robert could have married from about age 20 (c. 1878) up to the late 1890s (James and Betsy would need to be old enough to appear as children in 1911). Search England and Wales Marriage Registration Index 1837–2005 (FamilySearch collection 2285732) and FreeBMD/LancashireBMD marriages 1837–2010.

Traces Robert Brierley (~33) with wife Ellen in 1891 (FamilySearch collection 1865747), confirming the couple's marriage had taken place by this date and showing any children born before 1891. Bridges the gap between the 1881 solo record and the 1911 household with James and Betsy.

Traces Robert Brierley (~43) with Ellen in 1901 (FamilySearch collection 1888129). Confirms continued Rochdale residence and shows the family composition a decade before 1911 — James and Betsy should begin appearing here if born by 1901. Confirms identity continuity across the census sequence.

Fallback for pli_002 (civil birth registration). If no GRO birth entry is found for Robert Brierley in 1858 — possible given pre-1875 registration gaps noted in loc_001 — search the Lancashire parish baptism registers. England, Lancashire, Parish Registers 1538–1910 (FamilySearch collection 1465701) indexes Anglican baptisms; also search England, Lancashire Non-Conformist Church Records 1647–1996 (collection 3656808) given Rochdale's strong Nonconformist community (Baptists, Methodists, Independents were prevalent per loc_001). A baptism entry naming Abel Brierley as father would substitute for the civil registration. Search Rochdale St Chad and its ~20 chapelries; per loc_001, part of this parish straddles into Yorkshire — also check Yorkshire registers if not found in Lancashire.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: The second plan (pl_002) completed two targeted searches — church baptism registers for Robert Brierley b.1866 with father Abel (pli_010, negative across five searches in collections 1465701 and 1788853), and marriage registration for Ellen Brierley to identify her late husband (pli_011). That marriage search yielded a decisive positive: the GRO Marriage Index (src_005, log_032) confirms Ellen married Griffith Brierley in 1859 at Rochdale — not Abel Brierley. The 1891 census (src_004) shows Robert b.~1866 as son of widowed Ellen (b.1833); her husband was Griffith, not Abel. Combined with three censuses (1891, 1901, 1911) consistently placing this Robert's birth at ~1866 (not 1858 as in the tree's Robert Lord), and the 1861 Abel Brierley household search finding no son Robert, the evidence is conclusive: the 1911 Rochdale Robert Brierley (son of Griffith and Ellen Brierley, b.~1866) is NOT the tree person Robert Lord (b.1858, purported son of Abel Brierley). The hypothesis is refuted on both components — birth year and parentage. Civil registration began 1 July 1837 (FamilySearch England Civil Registration wiki); Robert's 1866 birth falls within the registration period. The GRO birth certificate was not obtained, but the marriage finding makes its expected content predictable: it would name Griffith (or a different father) — no unsearched avenue could plausibly revive the Abel hypothesis.

Lancashire/Yorkshire cross-search noted; Rochdale straddles both counties per loc_001 and was factored in.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. The 1901 census (src_003) and 1911 census (src_001) are original records — an enumerator-completed return and a householder-completed schedule respectively. The 1891 census (src_004) is an original enumerator return. The GRO Marriage Index (src_005) and GRO Birth Index (src_002) are derivatives, but the Anglican marriage register post-1837 is an exact duplicate of the civil certificate (per the England Civil Registration wiki), and the marriage index suffices to establish the identity of Ellen's husband. The critical refutations rest on the census originals.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Three independently-created census records (1891, 1901, 1911) with different enumerators and informants all place Robert Brierley's birth at ~1866. The GRO Birth Index (src_002) corroborates 1866, Rochdale. The GRO Marriage Index (src_005) independently establishes Ellen's husband as Griffith Brierley (1859 Rochdale). These are genuinely independent sources with different creation processes and institutional origins, all pointing to the same refutation.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. At least three original records with primary information: 1911 census householder-completed schedule (src_001, primary for household composition); 1901 census original enumerator return (src_003, primary for residence and family structure); 1891 census original enumerator return (src_004, primary for Ellen's widowed status and Robert's relationship as her son). Marriage assertions in src_005 carry primary information_quality (self-reported by the parties).
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. The core conflict — the tree's Robert Lord recorded as b.1858 vs. the 1911 Rochdale Robert Brierley consistently recorded as b.~1866 across three censuses and the birth index — is resolved by the preponderance of evidence: all independent sources agree on 1866, and the tree's 1858 figure is an unsupported prior. No source names Abel Brierley as the father of the 1911 householder. The marriage record (Ellen + Griffith Brierley, 1859) closes the paternity question. No unresolved conflicts remain that would block this conclusion.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Civil registration began 1 July 1837 (England Civil Registration wiki, FamilySearch). The 1866 birth falls squarely within the registration period. The GRO birth certificate for Robert Brierley b.1866 was not obtained, but its expected content is now predictable given the marriage finding: it would name Griffith Brierley as father (or another father — either outcome refutes the Abel hypothesis). No unsearched record type could plausibly establish Abel as father of the 1911 Rochdale Robert Brierley: the 1861 Abel Brierley household search was negative; all Robert+Abel baptism searches were negative; Ellen's marriage to Griffith is documented. No plausible avenue remains that could revive the hypothesis posed in q_001.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Argument: Was the 1911 Rochdale Robert Brierley Born in 1858 as a Son of Abel Brierley, Making Him the Same Person as Robert Lord (GSPY-NFZ)?

**Conclusion: Disproved.** The 1911 Rochdale Robert Brierley is not the tree person Robert Lord (GSPY-NFZ, birth year 1858, purported son of Abel Brierley). The hypothesis is refuted on two independent components — birth year and parentage — each of which, standing alone, would be sufficient to sever the proposed identity; together, they are conclusive.

---

### Research Question

The tree person Robert Lord (GSPY-NFZ) is recorded with a birth year of 1858 and is asserted to be a son of Abel Brierley. The 1911 England and Wales census at Rochdale records a Robert Brierley as head of household — with wife Ellen and children James and Betsy — bearing a birth year of 1866. The question asks whether these are the same man.

---

### Evidence Analyzed

**Source 1 — 1911 England and Wales Census, Robert Brierley household.**
"England and Wales, Census, 1911," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X4M4-HG9 : accessed 16 September 2026), entry for Robert Brierley and household, Rochdale, Lancashire, England, United Kingdom; schedule reference RG14/24636/0319; FamilySearch, citing The National Archives of the UK, Kew, Surrey, England.

This derivative index (original schedule not examined) records Robert Brierley as head of household, male, married, born approximately 1866 at Rochdale, Lancashire, occupation cotton mill stripper and grinder. His wife is Ellen Brierley (b. ~1869, Rochdale); his children in the household are James Brierley (b. ~1895, Rochdale) and Betsy Brierley (b. ~1899, Rochdale). The 1911 census is distinctive in that it used original householder-completed schedules, making the recorded birth year the direct statement of the head himself. A birth year of 1866 is recorded — not 1858.

Source classification: derivative/indeterminate information/direct evidence for household facts. Residence at Rochdale in 1911 carries primary information quality (census enumerator as witness to the physical location of the household).

**Source 2 — England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837-2008.**
"England and Wales, Birth Registration Index, 1837-2008", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:2XS7-L43 : accessed 16 September 2026), entry for Robert Brierley, 1866.

This derivative index of the General Register Office civil birth registration records an entry for Robert Brierley, male, born 1866 in the Rochdale registration district. The original birth certificate (which would name the father) was not examined. The index alone cannot confirm the father's name. This source is classified as derivative/indeterminate information/direct evidence. It corroborates the 1866 birth year independently of the censuses.

**Source 3 — 1901 England and Wales Census, Robert Brierley household.**
"England and Wales, Census, 1901", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X9G3-FRG : accessed 16 September 2026), entry for Robert Brierley and Ellen Brierley, 31 March 1901.

This derivative index records Robert Brierley as head of household, male, married, born approximately 1866 at Rochdale, Lancashire, occupation cotton mill stripper and grinder (identical to 1911). Wife Ellen Brierley (b. ~1869) and children James Brierley (b. ~1895) and Betsy Brierley (b. ~1899) are present. Birth year derived from age column — classified as indirect evidence in this source, since census age columns record age-at-census, not a directly stated birth year. Still, the derived birth year of ~1866 is consistent with both the 1911 census and the birth index. The occupation match across both censuses (1901 and 1911) is a strong internal consistency marker confirming these records describe the same man.

**Source 4 — 1891 England and Wales Census, Ellen Brierley household.**
"England and Wales, Census, 1891," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QB58-WW2 : accessed 16 September 2026), entry for Robert Brierley in household of Ellen Brierley, Rochdale St Chad, Lancashire, England; FamilySearch, from General Register Office census returns, 1891.

This is the pivotal source for the parentage refutation. In 1891, Robert Brierley (b. ~1866, single, occupation cardroom jobber cotton) appears as a son in the household of Ellen Brierley — who is head of household, widowed, born approximately 1833 at Rochdale. This Ellen is demonstrably distinct from Robert's later wife Ellen (b. ~1869): the age gap is 36 years, she is designated head of household rather than wife, and she is widowed rather than married. This Ellen is Robert Brierley's mother. Her status as widow establishes that her late husband — Robert's father — was deceased before 1891.

Source classification: derivative/indeterminate information/direct evidence for name and relationship facts; primary information/direct evidence for residence.

**Source 5 — England and Wales Marriage Registration Index, 1837-2005.**
"England and Wales, Marriage Registration Index, 1837-2005", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:2D7X-S7J : accessed 2026-09-16), entry for Griffith Brierley and Ellen, 1859, Rochdale, Lancashire, England.

This GRO marriage index entry — derivative/primary information/direct evidence, with Griffith Brierley and Ellen as parties who would have furnished the information themselves — records that a man named **Griffith Brierley** married a woman named Ellen in 1859 at Rochdale, Lancashire. Robert Brierley was born in 1866 in Rochdale. A woman named Ellen who married a man surnamed Brierley in Rochdale in 1859 and was widowed before 1891, with a son Robert born 1866, is the widowed Ellen Brierley of the 1891 census with a probability that admits no serious alternative in the evidence record. Robert Brierley's father was **Griffith Brierley**, not Abel Brierley.

The bride's maiden surname is not indexed in this GRO entry; the original certificate was not examined. The index is nonetheless sufficient to identify the groom's surname (Brierley, matching the family surname), the bride's given name (Ellen, matching), the year (1859, consistent with a son born 1866), and the place (Rochdale, consistent with all census records).

---

### Weighing the Evidence

**Component 1 — Birth year.**

The tree records Robert Lord (GSPY-NFZ) with a birth year of 1858. Every independent source consulted for the 1911 Rochdale householder gives a birth year of ~1866:

- 1911 census (self-reported on a householder schedule): 1866
- 1901 census (age-derived): ~1866
- 1891 census (age-derived): ~1866
- GRO Birth Registration Index (registration year): 1866

Three independently created census records with different enumerators and informants, plus a civil registration index from a separate institutional process, all agree on 1866. An 8-year discrepancy between 1866 and 1858 is not the product of rounding or approximation error: even allowing for age misreporting in census records (which typically varies by one or two years), an 8-year gap across four independent sources all consistent with each other is incompatible with a shared identity. This alone disproves identity.

**Component 2 — Parentage.**

The hypothesis requires that Robert Brierley's father was Abel Brierley. The evidence is uniformly against this:

- The 1891 census shows Robert living with his widowed mother Ellen Brierley (b. ~1833). His mother's maiden surname is unknown, but her husband — Robert's father — had the surname Brierley (as Robert carries it) and was deceased before 1891.
- The GRO Marriage Registration Index identifies **Griffith** Brierley (not Abel) as the man who married an Ellen in Rochdale in 1859 — seven years before Robert's 1866 birth, and in the same place where Robert's entire documented life is located. No other Brierley husband for this Ellen is evidenced.
- The 1861 England census search for an Abel Brierley household at Rochdale found no son named Robert. All baptism register searches (Lancashire Parish Registers, collection 1465701; Manchester Parish Registers, collection 1788853) for Robert with father Abel were negative across five separate searches.
- No source consulted in this project names Abel Brierley as the father of Robert Brierley. The Abel hypothesis rests entirely on a tree-entered prior with no documentary foundation in the record set.

**Component 3 — Surname.**

The tree person is Robert Lord; the 1911 householder is Robert Brierley. The conclusion was aware from the outset that the name change needed explanation: neither the record set nor the tree carries any document explaining how a man born Robert Lord came to be recorded as Robert Brierley throughout his life (1891, 1901, and 1911 censuses). No marriage record, adoption record, or other instrument producing a surname change was found. Identity cannot be asserted when the surname conflict is unexplained and every independently searched record supports the surname Brierley as the man's birth surname (consistent with his father having the surname Brierley).

---

### Negative Search Results

The following targeted searches returned no results supporting the Abel Brierley hypothesis:

- 1861 England census, Abel Brierley household at Rochdale: searched, no son Robert found.
- Lancashire Parish Registers 1538-1910 (collection 1465701), baptism of Robert with father Abel Brierley: negative across five searches.
- Manchester Parish Registers (collection 1788853), same search parameters: negative.
- Any source naming Abel Brierley as father of a Robert Brierley born approximately 1858 or 1866: none found.

Negative search results in the context of a declared-exhaustive research plan constitute meaningful negative evidence: the absence of any corroborating document for the Abel hypothesis, across multiple searched record types, strengthens the refutation.

---

### Limitations and Unsearched Records

Two original documents were not examined that would add precision but would not change the conclusion:

1. **GRO birth certificate for Robert Brierley, 1866, Rochdale.** This would confirm the father's name. Given that every other line of evidence points to Griffith Brierley as father, this certificate's expected content is predictable. Even in the unlikely event that the father is listed as a man other than Griffith, it would not be Abel — no source places Abel in this family. Obtaining this certificate would add confirmation of the father's name; it cannot revive the Abel hypothesis.

2. **GRO marriage certificate for Griffith Brierley and Ellen, 1859, Rochdale.** This would supply Ellen's maiden surname and both parties' fathers' names, providing further corroboration. Its absence does not weaken the identification of Griffith as the father: the convergence of the marriage index, the 1891 census widow status, and the consistent birth year evidence is sufficient.

The research is declared exhaustive for the purposes of this question. No unsearched avenue could plausibly revive the hypothesis.

---

### Conclusion

The preponderance of evidence — four independent sources placing Robert Brierley's birth at ~1866, the GRO marriage index identifying Griffith Brierley (not Abel) as the husband of the family's widowed mother Ellen, five negative searches for any Robert with father Abel, and an unexplained surname divergence — establishes with certainty well above the `probable` threshold that the 1911 Rochdale Robert Brierley is NOT the tree person Robert Lord (GSPY-NFZ, b. 1858, son of Abel Brierley). The hypothesis posed in q_001 is disproved.

Consequently, the children James Brierley and Betsy Brierley enumerated with the 1911 Rochdale household are the children of Robert Brierley (b. ~1866, son of Griffith Brierley) and his wife Ellen — they are not children of Robert Lord (GSPY-NFZ) and cannot be attributed to that tree person on the basis of this evidence.

## Research Conclusion: `disproved`

**Question:** Was the Robert Brierley enumerated at Rochdale in the 1911 census — with wife Ellen and children James and Betsy — the same man as Robert Lord (b. 1858, son of Abel Brierley)?

**Answer: No.** They are two different men.

### Evidence

| Source | Finding |
|--------|---------|
| 1911 census (src_001) | Robert Brierley, b. **1866**, stripper & grinder, wife Ellen (b.1869), children James (b.1895) and Betsy (b.1899) — Rochdale |
| 1901 census (src_003) | Same Robert Brierley, b. **1866**, with same wife and children |
| 1891 census (src_004) | Robert Brierley, b. **1866**, single, living with his **widowed mother Ellen** (b.1833) — four siblings also present |
| GRO birth index (src_002) | Robert Brierley registered **1866**, Rochdale |
| GRO marriage index (src_005) | Ellen married **Griffith Brierley** in **1859 in Rochdale** — not Abel Brierley |

### Why this is conclusive

1. **Birth year gap:** Four independent sources across 20 years consistently record this Robert as born ~1866, not 1858. An 8-year discrepancy cannot be attributed to normal recording variance.
2. **Father's identity:** His widowed mother Ellen married **Griffith Brierley**, not Abel Brierley. Robert b.1866 was therefore the son of Griffith and Ellen Brierley.
3. **Abel's household (1861):** No son named Robert appears.
4. **No baptism linking father Abel:** Five searches across Lancashire and Manchester church registers found no baptism of a Robert Brierley with father Abel near 1866.

**The children James (b.1895) and Betsy (b.1899) are Griffith and Ellen Brierley's grandchildren — not children of the tree's Robert Lord.**
